# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the 24 h re-anchored post-fix prefill-recovery window measured
at its completion, so the epic closes on a fully-covered, gap-free log set and
LP-0MVLHMAWV008EKTI AC3 (delegated here) carries the completion verdict.

## Context

- LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2 AC1 requires the measurement JSON + hourly table for the full
  window pasted into that item; the window is time-gated and completes
  **2026-10-24 22:04:14 IST** — this item is runnable only from that moment.
- LP-0MVLHMAWV008EKTI (restart-safe logging, on dev) guarantees the window is fully
  covered across restarts: 22:04:14-anchored coverage has stayed `gaps: []` through
  four mid-window restarts (23:48, 00:08, 00:33, 10:35) and three rotations. This item
  verifies the full span and reports the verdict back.
- LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2 also awaits the producer decision on AC3 semantics
  (LP-0MVLHMCN6003GAMD — lease-active denial vs wedge signature); if that decision is
  still pending, record the findings and the open question rather than blocking.

## Proposed change

1. At/after 2026-10-24 22:04:14 IST run:

   ```bash
   cd /home/rgardler/projects/llm
   python3 scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure \
       --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
       --since '2026-10-23 22:04:14' --until '2026-10-24 22:04:14' --json
   ```

2. Render the hourly table over the same window
   (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`).
   Note: any restart after 10:35:04 will archive the in-between window without
   loss (LP-0MVLHMAWV008EKTI) — record the restart, do not re-anchor.

3. Paste the measurement JSON + hourly table into LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2, and post the
   `coverage.verdict_met` result here, closing LP-0MVLHMAWV008EKTI AC3.

4. Check the parent's AC2–AC4 signals in the window: zero-eval thrash hours
   (>=10 attempts, 0 served), `reason=local_lease_active` fallback count,
   at least one client-delivered `Stream finished ... provider=local`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The measurement JSON and hourly table for the full window
   (2026-10-23 22:04:14 → 2026-10-24 22:04:14) are pasted into
   LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2 and summarised here.
2. `coverage.verdict_met` is `true` (or, if false, the exact gap is reported with
   file names and timestamps and a regression item is filed with a blocking edge on
   the epic LP-0MVKN9IRP003XJH6).
3. Findings for the parent's AC2 (thrash hours), AC3 (lease-active denials — see
   LP-0MVLHMCN6003GAMD for the semantics decision) and AC4 (local stream delivered)
   are recorded with log excerpts.
4. LP-0MVLHMAWV008EKTI AC3 is closed here with the coverage verdict.

## Key Files

- scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py
- scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py
- .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py
- docs/dev/prefill-recovery-verification.md

## Deliverables

24 h measurement comment (report figures + log excerpts) on LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2;
coverage verdict closing LP-0MVLHMAWV008EKTI AC3; regression items if needed.

data.title: Conduct the 24 h re-anchored prefill-recovery measurement (runnable from 2026-10-24 22:04:14 IST)

data.description:
## Problem statement

Local admission is scheduled **per request** against a 2-slot llama-server pool
with no session→slot tenancy and no check of the *actual* reusable prefix, so
any session can land on another session's slot and lose the resident KV. 27
distinct sessions cycled through 2 slots in ~5.4 h on 2026-10-24; aggregate
prefix reuse was 26.1 % and the median for prompts >20k tokens was **15.6 %**
(28 of 227 fully cold), and 160 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` cancellations in
5.4 h wasted ~780k prefill tokens (~93 % of local compute in the window).

The routing estimator cannot see this: `cached_ratio` is predicted from the
session's own snapshot sidecar (`proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`) and is
structurally wrong under contention (`cached_ratio ≈ 0.99` predicted for
requests that then prefilled from `n_past=738`), which is why the 38k cold cap
never fired. The counter-example that proves it is slot churn rather than
GPU incapacity: the identical 49,103-token prompt scored `n_past=738` on its
first attempt (deadline-cancelled) and **100 % reuse (`n_past=49103`)** on the
immediate same-prompt retry, before another session trashed the slot.

## Users

- **Primary — local-work sessions (herdr / opencode clients):** multi-turn
  coding sessions with large, mostly-resident context that today lose their
  prefix on nearly every turn.
- **Secondary — the proxy operator:** needs local throughput without paying
  remote tokens for work the GPU could have done, and needs a truthful signal
  when local admission declines.
- **Tertiary — the capacity/usage analyst:** consumes the usage report to
  attribute local vs remote dispatch and resident-vs-evicted reuse.

User stories:

- *As a multi-turn local session*, my second and later turns should resume
  from my resident prefix instead of a cold prefill that consumes my whole
  deadline.
- *As the proxy operator*, a cold prompt that cannot finish inside the prefill
  deadline must not be admitted just because a prediction said it would be
  cheap.
- *As the operator*, I want to see, per admission decision, the measured
  reusable prefix and which session owned the slot, so residency regressions
  are visible without forensics.
- *As a client whose connection died*, I must not leave a dead session holding
  the pool; the proxy alone reaps me within a bounded window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Resident-prefix admission gate.** Before a local dispatch of a large prompt is admitted, the router computes the session's *actual* reusable prefix from live slot state and admits only when `reuse_ratio = min(context_tokens, estimated_tokens) / estimated_tokens` is `>= local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` (default `0.5`, `0` disables). Otherwise it skips local with reason `resident_prefix_insufficient` and the chain falls through as it does today. Cold prompts above the admission budget from non-resident sessions are never admitted. *Measured by:* unit tests over stubbed slot snapshots + a replay fixture of the 2026-10-24 window asserting zero over-budget cold admissions.
- **AC2 — Session tenancy ("N tenants, 2 slots").** At most `local_session_tenants` distinct sessions (default: the slot count, i.e. 2) may hold a local reservation for a large prompt at once. A new session's large prompt is admitted only when a slot is free of other sessions' prefixes, or when the resident session's tenancy has idle-lapsed (`local_session_tenancy_idle_seconds`, default derived from the existing adaptive dispatch lease). Beyond that bound the request follows the normal chain rather than evicting a resident session.
- **AC3 — Live-prefix pricing (re-scoped).** The cold-cache gate (`provider._should_skip_local`) prices `new_tokens` from the **live** measurement used by AC1 rather than the predicted sidecar ratio, so the new-token cap is evaluated against real prefill work. The budget constant itself is owned by `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` (25k) and is consumed, not redefined, here. *Measured by:* zero admissions whose live `new_tokens > cold threshold` unless idle-exempt.
- **AC4 — Deadline/thrash regression (re-anchored), verified by a mandatory follow-up work item.** On a 24 h window measured **after** `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` is deployed, scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events are >= 90 % below that window's own re-anchored baseline; genuine GPU-speed misses are out of scope. A cancellation counts as *scheduling-attributed* when either the live `reuse_ratio` at admission was below `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`, or `slot_owner_session` changed between admission and the deadline event (i.e. the prefix was evicted by another session). The 2026-10-24 figures (160 events / 5.4 h, ~780k wasted tokens) remain the historical reference only. **Verification is executed by a separate follow-up work item, and creating that item is a deliverable of this one (not optional):**
- Title format: `24 h AC4 verification of resident-prefix admission — run no earlier than <ISO-8601 UTC instant>`. The instant in the title is the earliest the review can run: the **later** of this item's deploy and `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`'s deploy, **+ 24 h**. Until this item ships, the title carries the provable lower bound (now + 24 h); the implementing agent MUST retitle it with the concrete deploy-derived instant on ship.
- Description records the pinned measurement window (start/end UTC), the baseline re-anchoring query for that window, the `proxy-usage-analysis` invocation, and the scheduling-attributed classifier above.
- Linked `discovered-from:LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG` and related to `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D`; assigned to the operator's triage queue.
- AC4 is **not** satisfied by the implementing agent's own measurements: it is satisfied only when the follow-up item reports its 24 h result.
- **AC5 — Observability.** Every admission denial and admission logs `n_past_actual`, `estimated_tokens`, `reuse_ratio`, `slot_owner_session`, and the decision (`admit` / `resident_prefix_insufficient` / `tenant_limit`) at `routing_skip_local` / `routing_hop` level, and the `proxy-usage-analysis` report surfaces resident-vs-evicted reuse splits and slot-owner churn per session.
- **AC6 — Tenancy reservations are leases, not locks.** Reservations follow the existing dispatch-record lease pattern: held only while real activity is observed (data chunks, prefill progress, or a live client confirmed by the poll-cadence `request.is_disconnected()`), TTL refresh bounded by the 180 s no-progress watchdog and the 900 s lifetime ceiling, never extended by a merely open upstream socket. Reclaim uses the existing ~10 s `_dispatch_cleanup_loop`: within seconds when a disconnect is observed (release record, pop prefill marker, free slot assignment, cancel the captured upstream `stream_cm`) and within <= 180 s for a silent half-open drop; no path leaves a dead session gating the pool beyond those bounds (the 2026-10-23 ~5.5–6 min `local_lease_active` window is the regression baseline). On reclaim the evicted session's KV snapshot is saved (`slot_<id>.bin`, subject to pool-size and busy gates) so a returning client restores warm instead of prefilling cold. The proxy is the sole owner of abandonment reaping; no client protocol change is required.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit coverage for: resident accept / non-resident reject, ratio boundary, tenancy bound, unknown-`context_tokens` fallback ladder, predicted-vs-actual divergence, and both reclaim bounds. Integration coverage replays the 2026-10-24 thrash fixture and asserts (a) no cold admission above the budget without a resident prefix and (b) task 92383/92422 classify as resident on retry. All tests run through the test skill.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** `proxy/config.yaml` documents every new knob (defaults, 0-disables semantics, interaction with `local_idle_admit_*` and `contention_queue_*`); `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `docs/dev/cached-ratio-prefix-credit.md` and `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` describe the admission ladder and the "read the cached slot snapshot, never a synchronous `/slots` call" constraint.
- **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- **`/slots` must not be queried on the admission hot path.** Under a
  prompt-processing batch llama-server holds `/slots` for >15 s (measured 8.7 s
  then >15 s, vs the 1 s status timeout) — see `LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC`. AC1 must
  therefore read the in-memory snapshot already maintained every ~1 s by
  `_periodic_broadcast_loop()` (`observability._last_slot_details_cache`,
  TTL-coalesced `/slots` poll, 5 s failure backoff) plus
  `session._slot_owners`; any synchronous upstream call is prohibited.
- **Fail-open on unknown state.** A missing/stale snapshot, an unreported
  `context_tokens` (llama b8782 dropped `n_past`), or a cache older than the
  freshness bound must not turn into a hard local outage: fall back to the
  session-owns-slot check, then to today's predicted-ratio decision.
- **No change to** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (stays a backstop;
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` owns the 90→110 change) and no change to
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills`.
- **No live slot-count change** here: widening the snapshot pool is evaluated
  separately in `LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`, and adding llama slots shrinks per-slot
  context (262,144 → 87,381 at 3 slots), excluding the long-context sessions
  that dominate this workload.
- **Idle-awareness must keep working.** `local_idle_admit_enabled`
  (`LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J`) deliberately overrides the economic bypass when the
  GPU is idle; the new gate must not silently disable that behaviour.
- `contention_queue_*` semantics are unchanged: a request denied by AC1/AC2
  does not consume the queue budget differently from today's bypass path.

## Existing state

- Admission is per-request: `router_helpers._try_acquire_local_dispatch()`
  keeps N concurrent dispatch leases (`local_active_queries`,
  `local_dispatch_records`, no-preemption cooldown), which bounds *in-flight*
  requests but not *which* sessions occupy the pool over time.
- The economic gate is `provider._should_skip_local()`: a hard
  `warm_cache_threshold` cap plus `new_tokens = estimated_tokens *
  (1 - cached_ratio)` compared to the cold threshold, where `cached_ratio`
  comes from `_last_cached_ratio` and the snapshot sidecar
  (`slot_cache_ratio.py`, safety margin 0.9, prefix-fingerprint validated).
- Slot ownership/persistence already exists: `session._slot_owners`
  (`(endpoint, slot_id) -> session_id`), `_slot_id_for_session`,
  `_free_slot_assignment`, `_save_slot_snapshot` / `_restore_slot_snapshot`
  with per-slot failure cooldowns and `session_slot_skip_when_busy: true`.
- Live slot state is already collected: `observability._query_slots_detail()`
  (single-flight, 1 s TTL, 5 s failure backoff) feeds
  `_last_slot_details_cache`; log-derived progress (`_slot_progress_cache`,
  60 s max age) supplements builds that dropped `n_past`.
- Mitigations already shipped: post-deadline thrash cooldown
  (`LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL`, 10 min default), no-progress watchdog + prefill
  liveness extension (`LP-0MUCEFB8E003YVFF`, `LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O`),
  atomic reservations (`admission_reserve.py`).
- Measured gap: none of the above consults the *live* resident prefix, and
  none bounds the number of distinct sessions contending for the pool.

## Desired change

1. **Residency view (shared, in-memory).** Build a small read-only projection
   of `(slot_id, owner_session, context_tokens, is_processing, age)` from
   `_last_slot_details_cache` + `session._slot_owners`, exposed as one function
   used by AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5. No new poller, no upstream call, no lock
   inversion (read under a snapshot copy).
2. **Admission ladder** in `_should_skip_local` / the local dispatch path:
   (i) hard `warm_cache_threshold` cap (unchanged); (ii) **resident-prefix
   gate** (AC1) with the fallback ladder — `context_tokens` known → measured
   ratio; unknown but session owns the slot → treat as resident (restore
   path); otherwise → non-resident; (iii) **tenancy** check (AC2); (iv) cold
   pricing from live `new_tokens` (AC3); (v) existing idle-exempt override
   stays last, so an idle GPU still serves cold work.
3. **Tenancy as a lease** registered alongside the existing dispatch records
   (AC6), reaped by `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` and the no-progress watchdog, so
   no new lifecycle machinery is introduced.
4. **Logging + report** (AC5) using the existing structured log lines rather
   than a new sink.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_should_skip_local()` cold pricing (AC1/AC3),
  local dispatch path, `_last_cached_ratio`; new admission ladder entry point.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `_last_slot_details_cache`,
  `_query_slots_detail()`, `_slot_context_tokens()`, `_slot_progress_cache`
  (source of the live residency view; TTL/backoff invariants).
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — `_slot_owners` registry, `_slot_id_for_session`,
  `_free_slot_assignment`, `_save_slot_snapshot` / `_restore_slot_snapshot`
  (tenancy ↔ slot ownership, AC6 reclaim + snapshot on eviction).
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch()` tenancy
  bound, `_release_local_dispatch()`, `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch()`,
  prefill-thrash cooldown interaction.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — reservation verdict should consume the
  same residency view so `POST /llama/local/reserve` and the guard agree.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `evaluate_admission` ETA unchanged, but the
  admission verdict feeding it carries live `new_tokens`.
- `proxy/proxy/disconnect_reaper.py` — abandonment observation used by AC6.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — new `server.*` knobs: `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`
  (0.5), `local_session_tenants` (default = slot count),
  `local_session_tenancy_idle_seconds`.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `test_session_slot_affinity_continuity.py`, `test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`,
  `test_local_idle_admission.py`, `test_lease_truthfulness.py`,
  `test_prefill_thrash_cooldown.py`, `test_prefill_eta_occupancy.py` —
  extend for AC1/AC2/AC3/AC6.
- `proxy/scripts/replay_prefill_occupancy.py` — extend as the 2026-10-24
  replay fixture driver (AC7).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — AC5
  resident-vs-evicted report section.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `docs/dev/cached-ratio-prefix-credit.md`,
  `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` — AC8.

## Non-goals

- No change to `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` or
  `local_max_concurrent_prefills`.
- No live slot-count increase (see `LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`) and no change to the
  snapshot pool size here.
- No client-side cooperation for abandonment (proxy-owned reaping only).
- No attempt to make llama.cpp's native context-checkpoint restore rate a
  scheduling signal (`docs/dev/restore-rate-metric-fix-ranking.md`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: admission starvation.** A strict residency gate could refuse local
  for most large prompts, shifting cost to remote. *Mitigation:* the idle-exempt
  override stays last in the ladder, the gate is configurable (0 disables),
  and AC5 logging makes the shift visible within one report cycle.
- **Risk: stale snapshot decisions.** A 1 s TTL snapshot can be wrong exactly
  at a slot switch. *Mitigation:* reason about ownership (authoritative
  in-process registry) rather than throughput, and fail-open on unknown state.
- **Risk: `/slots` unobservability repeats** (`LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC`), leaving
  `context_tokens` unknown. *Mitigation:* the fallback ladder + log-derived
  progress cache; the feature must remain correct when the number is absent.
- **Risk: tenancy + single-flight interaction** can make a session wait behind
  its own earlier turn; *Mitigation:* same-session re-acquisition is always
  permitted (existing lease semantics), and the tenancy check only gates
  *new* sessions.
- **Risk: the 0.5 default is aggressive for this workload.** Measured median
  reuse is 15.6 % for prompts >20k, so a 0.5 default may refuse most large
  prompts initially. *Mitigation:* one knob, `0` disables, staged observation
  via AC5 logs before the AC4 window; the ladder still admits same-slot
  residents and idle-exempt work.
- **Assumption:** the local pool stays at 2 slots and
  `session_slot_pool_size: 2` for the duration of this work; a pool-size change
  (`LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`) invalidates the tenancy default and the AC4 baseline.
- **Assumption:** `session._slot_owners` stays accurate under churn — verified
  by `LP-0MTIHWYGJ006YS6X` continuity tests; new tests extend them.
- **Assumption:** the 25k budget from `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` is the constant
  consumed by AC3; if that item changes scope, AC3's threshold follows it.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "more slots", snapshot-pool widening, and checkpoint
  tuning are adjacent opportunities — they stay linked work items
  (`LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5`), not additions to this brief.

## Testability

Unit tests stub the residency view (slot snapshot + owner map) and assert the
ladder: resident accept, non-resident reject, ratio boundary at exactly
`local_resident_prefix_min_ratio`, unknown-`context_tokens` fallback, tenancy
bound with same-session re-entry, live-vs-predicted divergence (predicted 0.99,
actual 0.015 → reject), and both AC6 reclaim bounds (observed disconnect
releases within one cleanup cycle; silent drop released by the 180 s watchdog,
never the 900 s ceiling). Integration replays the 2026-10-24 thrash window
fixture through the guard and asserts no over-budget cold admission without a
resident prefix, and that task 92383/92422 classify as resident on the retry.
The 24 h AC4 comparison is a post-deploy analysis (`proxy-usage-analysis`)
executed by the mandated follow-up work item, not a test-suite gate and not a
deliverable of this item's implementation session beyond creating that item.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` — **24 h AC4 verification of resident-prefix admission
  — run no earlier than 2026-10-26T00:51Z** (created by this intake as AC4's
  mandated verification vehicle; retitle to the deploy-derived instant on
  ship).
- `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` — Cold-prefill admission budget 25k + deadline 90→110 s
  (critical; owns the budget constant AC3 consumes and the baseline AC4
  re-anchors against).
- `LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5` — Evaluate widening `session_slot_pool_size` 2→4
  (alternative residency lever, explicitly out of scope here).
- `LP-0MVKUKFHH005UDWL` — Post-deadline prefill-thrash cooldown (existing
  mitigation; AC4 residual must be read alongside it).
- `LP-0MUCEFB8E003YVFF` — No-progress watchdog + progress-aware lease extension
  (AC6 lease baseline).
- `LP-0MVKUKFSO008GI6O` — Truthful lease and in-flight accounting (AC6
  "in-flight is not progress").
- `LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC` — `/slots` unobservable during long prefills (hard
  constraint on AC1's data source).
- `LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304` — Seed `cached_ratio` from the persisted slot snapshot
  (the prediction AC3 replaces with live measurement).
- `LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J` — Idle-aware local admission (override that must
  survive the new gate).
- `LP-0MQR75QYM001HAUB` — Slot thrashing reproduction (precedent evidence).
- `LP-0MTIHWYGJ006YS6X` — Session-slot affinity/ownership continuity (registry
  accuracy assumed by AC1/AC2).
- `LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV` — Second-turn `cached_ratio` scored 0.00 after a
  successful cold first local turn (bootstrap defect in `update_cached_ratio`;
  the prediction AC3 replaces).
- `LP-0MUYN2RD800889S2` — `tests/test_cold_start_admission.py::test_proxy_to_local_warm_bypasses_cold_cap`
  test-failure (completed) — the same test file the AC1/AC3 guard tests extend.

Related docs: `docs/dev/cached-ratio-prefix-credit.md`,
`docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`,
`docs/dev/save-restore-reuse-gap-root-cause.md`,
`docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md`,
`docs/dev/slot-thrashing-investigation/findings.md`,
`docs/dev/in-flight-lease-hold-characterisation.md`,
`proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D** – Cold-prefill admission budget 25k tokens + prefill deadline 90s -> 110s (open)
- **LP-0MUYN2RD800889S2** – [test-failure] tests/test_cold_start_admission.py::test_proxy_to_local_warm_bypasses_cold_cap — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: abandoned, aborts, absolute, ac1, ac2 (+264 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: 84k, absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+261 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When the resident-prefix check fails, does the request fall through to
  remote immediately, or queue for local?" — Answer (from the work item's AC1
  as authored, 2026-10-24): falls through to remote, matching today's
  `large_context_bypass` chain semantics; the queue budget is unchanged.
  Source: this work item's original description (AC1).
- Q: "Is the resident-prefix threshold a new knob, and at what default?" —
  Answer (from the work item's AC1): yes, configurable, default 50 % of
  `estimated_tokens`. Refined here to
  `server.local_resident_prefix_min_ratio: 0.5`, `0` disables.
  Source: this work item's original description (AC1) + `proxy/config.yaml`
  knob conventions.
- Q: "How is tenancy sized relative to the pool?" — Answer (from the work
  item's AC2): configurable, default <= slot count. Refined here to
  `server.local_session_tenants` defaulting to the resolved slot count.
  Source: this work item's original description (AC2).
- Q: "Should the budget cap live here?" — Answer (recorded 2026-10-25, session
  herdr-1792881165-2418241-523): no; the budget half ships in
  `LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D` and AC3 is re-scoped here to live-prefix pricing only,
  consuming that item's constant.
  Source: work-item comment LP-C0MVN3L6II0087BOD.
- Q: "Which evidence window should AC4 assert against?" — Answer (recorded
  2026-10-25): re-anchor to a post-budget-change 24 h window and measure the
  *residual* scheduling-attributed cancellations, not the absolute count; the
  2026-10-24 numbers become the historical reference.
  Source: work-item comment LP-C0MVN3LN8X0036MUF.
- Q: "May admission query `/slots` synchronously to get the live prefix?" —
  Answer (via repo research): no. `/slots` is held >15 s during prompt
  processing, so admission must read the ~1 s in-memory snapshot maintained by
  `_periodic_broadcast_loop()` and fail open when it is stale or lacks
  `context_tokens`. Research: `LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC`, `proxy/config.yaml`
  notes at `local_dispatch_lease_prefill_poll_seconds`,
  `observability._last_slot_details_cache`.
- Q: "Does a per-slot context reading exist for builds that dropped `n_past`?"

data.description:
## Goal

Stop admitting local prefills that cannot possibly finish before the prefill deadline, and widen the deadline enough to admit the largest genuinely feasible prompt:

1. **Cold-prefill admission budget = 25,000 tokens** of *new* (uncached / to-be-prefilled) tokens — a cap on what the GPU must actually compute, not on prompt size.
2. **`local_prefill_deadline_seconds`: 90 → 120 s.** Operator decision: keep the 25k budget and widen the time budget rather than reducing the prompt budget. At the measured 20–30k band rate (249 t/s) a 25k prefill is ~100 s, i.e. ~16 % margin under 120 s (and ~93 s / ~23 % margin at the band's p75 rate of ~270 t/s).

## Why (measured on this host, 2026-10-24/25)

Prompt-eval rates from `llama-server` logs (268 samples), size-dependent with a knee at ~27k:

| Prompt | Median rate | Prefill |
|---|---|---|
| 10–20k | 281 t/s | 36–71 s |
| 20–30k | 249 t/s | 80–100 s |
| 30–40k | 181 t/s | 165–210 s |
| 48k | 152 t/s | ~320 s |
| 63k | 114 t/s | ~563 s |

Consequences measured in the 2026-10-24 18:38–23:47 window: **160 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events**, 45 local tasks cancelled mid-prefill, **~780k of ~840k prefill tokens computed then discarded (~93 % waste)**. A 38k cold prefill (~210 s) can never fit a 90 s deadline; 25k (~100 s) fits 120 s with ~16 % margin.

## Concrete configuration proposal

All changes are in `proxy/config.yaml` (server section); nothing else changes.

| Key | Now | Proposed | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` | 90 | **120** | 25k cold ≈ 100 s at the measured 20–30k band rate (249 t/s): 90 s cancels it, 120 s admits it with ~16 % margin (~23 % at p75). Ordering stays `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds (60) < deadline (120) < local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds (840) < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds (900)` and below the client's 900 s queue deadline. |
| `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` *(new)* | — | **25000** (0 = disabled/rollback) | Hard cap on **new (to-be-prefilled) tokens** at admission, enforced on **every** admission path including `routing_idle_admit` (the economic bypass admitted 38 oversized requests in the window and is a direct leak). Refuse at admission with `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`; never dispatch-then-cancel. |
| `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens` *(new; currently the hard-coded `CONSERVATIVE_MIN_TOKENS = 32_768` in `prefill_eta.py`)* | 32768 | **20000** | Extend the existing p75 ETA percentile pricing down to cover the 25k budget band. p75 ≈ 270 t/s for 20–30k → 25k ≈ 93 s ≤ 0.95 × 120 = 114 s ✓ admitted; 30–40k band p75 ≈ 190 t/s → 132 s ✗ refused. This is what stops a band-slow 25k from slipping past the flat cap. |
| `local_admission_guard_budget_safety_fraction` *(new)* | — | **0.95** | Admit only when `eta_prefill_p75 ≤ 0.95 × deadline` (= 114 s at 120 s). Makes the budget deadline-relative instead of a bare token count, so future deadline changes stay consistent. |
| `local_admission_guard_reference_tokens` | 32000 | **25000** | Align the published-status reference prompt with the budget (one number instead of two). |
| `local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds` | 600 | **600 (unchanged)** | Now a backstop only; leave as-is. |
| `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` / `contention_queue_max_depth` | 60 / 8 | unchanged | Budget refusal happens before the queue. |
| Slot count / `session_slot_pool_size` | 2 / 2 | unchanged | Out of scope (see LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5). |

Left deliberately untouched: `cold_threshold` is *derived* (38000, from `_effective_large_context_thresholds` over per-slot ctx) and becomes a non-binding upper bound once the 25k measured budget exists; `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile` stays at 75 (it is simply applied from 20k upwards now).

Expected effect from the measured rates:

- >25k cold prompts (the 49k–93k thrash set): refused at admission → **zero** deadline cancellations for them (baseline: 160 events / 5.4 h, ~780k wasted tokens).
- 25k cold: 93–100 s, admitted and completed under the 120 s deadline.
- Warm requests (cached_ratio ≥0.9, e.g. 47k prompt / 549 new tokens): unchanged — the budget never binds.
- Residual deadline events: only genuine GPU-speed misses near the cap, priced at ≤114 s (p75).

Accepted trade-off of the 120 s choice: a near-budget prompt that *is* admitted and then lost consumes up to 114 s before the detour (vs 90 s today), +27 % worst-case waste per failed attempt — acceptable because the budget removes the systematically-doomed attempts, which were the source of the 93 % waste.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Budget:** `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens: 25000` caps the **new (prefilled) tokens** admitted for a local dispatch, on all admission paths (including idle/economic bypass). Over-budget requests are refused at admission (skip local, chain detours), never dispatched and never cancelled at the deadline.
- **AC2 — Deadline:** `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 120`. Enforce and assert the ordering `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds (60) < deadline (120) < local_dispatch_first_byte_timeout_seconds (840) < local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds (900)`, and keep the deadline strictly below the client's 900 s queue deadline (config-load assertion).
- **AC3 — Deadline-relative pricing:** budget admission uses p75 percentile ETA pricing from 20k tokens upwards (`local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens: 20000`) and admits only when `eta_prefill ≤ 0.95 × deadline` (114 s), so 25k at the 20–30k band is admitted and 25k in the 30–40k band is refused.
- **AC4 — Regression evidence:** over a 24 h window post-deploy, scheduling-attributed `prefill_deadline_exceeded` events are ≤10 % of the 2026-10-24 baseline (160 per 5.4 h), the AC7 eviction counter is zero for within-budget prompts, wasted-prefill tokens correspondingly reduced, and no increase in client-visible 503s / retries.
- **AC5 — Warm path unchanged:** warm requests remain admissible when total prompt size exceeds 25k (assert e.g. 47k prompt / 549 new tokens stays local).
- **AC6 — Documentation + rollback:** config comments state units, interaction with `cold_threshold`/`warm_threshold` and the admission guard, and the rollback values (budget 0, deadline 90, percentile-min 32768, safety fraction off).
- **AC7 — Record post-acceptance eviction as an ERROR (defect signal, not noise):** any local dispatch that was **accepted** (admitted, dispatch record created) and then **evicted before producing a first byte** must be recorded at **ERROR** log level — never WARNING/INFO — with a structured, machine-parseable event carrying at least: `session`, `reason` (`prefill_deadline` | `no_progress_watchdog` | `idle_timeout` | `orphan_cleanup` | `lease_evicted` | `slot_assignment_freed`), `estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `eta_prefill_s`, `elapsed_s`, `slot_id`, and the llama task id where known. This covers every release path an accepted dispatch can suffer, so eviction after acceptance is unambiguously an error condition rather than expected churn; refusals **before** acceptance stay at their current level (a budget/ETA refusal is normal operation, not an error). Ship with: (a) a dedicated monotonic counter and per-reason breakdown exposed in the `--json` summary and the `proxy-usage-analysis` report (`local_evictions_after_acceptance`), (b) an alerting threshold of >0 for evictions of within-budget prompts, and (c) a documented triage rule that any such ERROR is treated as a defect and filed as a `test-failure`-class work item — it is exactly the signal that the budget/pricing model is wrong for a prompt band.

## Tests

- Unit: budget boundary (24,999 admitted / 25,001 refused); warm bypass above 25k prompt size; deadline ordering assertion rejects a violating config; safety-fraction maths (114 s at 120 s); band-slow 25k refused via p75 pricing.
- Integration: fixture replay of the 2026-10-24 thrash window → zero admitted cold prompts >25k; every refused request detours with a logged reason.
- AC7 (eviction-after-acceptance is an ERROR): for **each** release path an accepted dispatch can take (`prefill_deadline`, `no_progress_watchdog`, `idle_timeout`, `orphan_cleanup`, `lease_evicted`, `slot_assignment_freed`), assert exactly one ERROR-level structured event is emitted with the required fields (session, reason, estimated_tokens, new_tokens, eta_prefill_s, elapsed_s, slot_id, llama task id where known), and assert none is emitted at WARNING/INFO. Assert the inverse too: a **pre-acceptance refusal** (budget / ETA / admission-guard) produces **no** ERROR (normal operation, no false alarms). Assert the counter increments once per eviction and that `local_evictions_after_acceptance` appears in the `--json` summary and in the `proxy-usage-analysis` report with its per-reason breakdown. Replay the 2026-10-24 thrash window as a regression fixture: with AC1/AC3 in force the counter must be 0 for within-budget prompts (any non-zero count fails the test, because it means the pricing model admitted a doomed dispatch).

## Relationships

- discovered-from: LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG (resident-prefix/tenancy admission). This item delivers the *budget* half of that item's AC3 ahead of the scheduler work and must ship independently; AC3 of LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG is to be re-scoped to the live-prefix pricing half when this lands.
- Do not increase the number of live slots in this item (per-slot ctx shrinks 131k → 87.4k at 3 slots).

## Goal

As the implementing agent for `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`, I need the failing-first unit
tests for the residency-aware admission ladder so that AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6 and AC7
(unit half) are pinned by executable, meaningful assertions before any production
code changes.

## Scope

New test module `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py` plus extensions
to existing suites. Tests are written against the *intended* API (a shared residency
view + the admission ladder), so they are added with
`@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="pending LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 / LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA / LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI / LP-0MVN4LADE001XD3M")` — the implement
skill's changed-scope gate therefore stays green, and the implementation items remove
the markers as each behaviour lands. No production code changes in this item.

Store-of-truth fixtures: a stubbed `_last_slot_details_cache` snapshot (slot_id,
is_processing, context_tokens, timestamp) and a stubbed `session._slot_owners` map.
No HTTP, no `/slots` call, no sleeps — every matrix cell is a pure function call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit coverage for: resident accept / non-resident reject, ratio boundary, tenancy bound, unknown-`context_tokens` fallback ladder, predicted-vs-actual divergence, and both reclaim bounds (this item authors those tests first).
- **AC7 (unit) — resident accept / non-resident reject:** tests assert the ladder admits a large prompt when the session's measured `reuse_ratio` is at/above `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` and skips local with reason `resident_prefix_insufficient` when below it.
- **AC1 — ratio boundary:** a dedicated test asserts the exact boundary (`reuse_ratio == local_resident_prefix_min_ratio` admits; one token below rejects) and that `local_resident_prefix_min_ratio: 0` disables the gate entirely.
- **AC1/AC7 — unknown-`context_tokens` fallback ladder:** tests cover (a) `context_tokens` known → measured ratio used, (b) `context_tokens` `None` but the session owns the slot → treated as resident (restore path), (c) neither → non-resident, falling back to today's predicted-ratio decision.
- **AC7 — predicted-vs-actual divergence:** a test pins the 2026-10-24 failure shape — predicted `cached_ratio` 0.99 with actual `n_past=738` of a 49,103-token prompt (actual reuse ≈ 0.015) must reject, proving the live measurement supersedes the sidecar prediction.
- **AC2 — tenancy bound:** tests assert at most `local_session_tenants` distinct sessions hold a large-prompt local reservation, that a same-session re-entry is always permitted, and that the denial reason is `tenant_limit`.
- **AC6 — both reclaim bounds:** tests assert an observed disconnect releases the reservation within one ~10 s `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` cycle, and a silent half-open drop is released by the 180 s no-progress watchdog and never only at the 900 s lifetime ceiling.
- **AC3 — live-prefix pricing:** a test asserts `new_tokens` is priced from the live measurement, so a request whose live `new_tokens` exceeds the cold threshold is refused even when the predicted ratio says it is cheap.
- All new tests run through the test skill (`/skill:test`) and collect cleanly with the rest of `proxy/tests`.

## Implementation sketch

- Build a small fixture factory returning
  `(slot_snapshot, slot_owners, now)` and reuse it across all matrix cells.
- Parametrise the ladder matrix over (context_tokens known/unknown, owner yes/no,
  ratio above/below/at boundary, tenants 1/2/3, snapshot fresh/stale).
- Do not fake production internals: stub only the two documented sources
  (`_last_slot_details_cache`, `session._slot_owners`).

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_local_resident_prefix_admission.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_session_slot_affinity_continuity.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_idle_admission.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_lease_truthfulness.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_cooldown.py`

## Dependencies

None — this is the test-first seed item; every implementation item depends on it.

## Assumptions

- `local_idle_admit_*` behaviour (`LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J`) must keep working, so the
  idle-exempt override is a test cell in this module (it stays last in the ladder).
- The 2026-10-24 divergence numbers (49,103-token prompt, `n_past=738`) are recorded
  in the parent item's problem statement and are usable as fixture constants.

## Decomposition (parent `LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG`)

Sibling items created by the plan session (2026-10-25). Execute in dependency order;
test items precede implementation items.

| Step | Item id | Scope | Depends on |
|------|---------|-------|------------|
| C1 | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H | Test harness (this item) | — |
| C2 | LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 | Shared residency view | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H |
| C3 | LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA | Resident-prefix gate + live pricing | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H, LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 |
| C4 | LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI | Session tenancy bound | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H, LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80 |
| C5 | LP-0MVN4LADE001XD3M | Tenancy lease reclaim | LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI |
| C6 | LP-0MVN4LANP0069QQM | Observability + usage report | LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA, LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI |
| C7 | LP-0MVN4LB5W005WJ71 | Thrash-window replay test | LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA, LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI, LP-0MVN4LANP0069QQM |
| C8 | LP-0MVN4LBOQ00743MG | Documentation | LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA, LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI, LP-0MVN4LADE001XD3M |
| C9 | LP-0MVN4LC7N005XH7P | Rollout + AC4 arming | LP-0MVN4L70T007C02H, LP-0MVN4L7AG003PC80, LP-0MVN4L7KT003XUBA, LP-0MVN4L7UX003KGTI, LP-0MVN4LADE001XD3M, LP-0MVN4LANP0069QQM, LP-0MVN4LB5W005WJ71, LP-0MVN4LBOQ00743MG |

- `C1` is the test-first seed: its new-behaviour tests carry
  `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="pending <impl-item-id>")` so every commit
  stays green; the implementation item that lands each behaviour removes its markers.
- Shared constraint across all items: read the cached slot snapshot
